subject: Edge multipath gateway options for Finovexa private deploy
messages:
From: Ari Walker <ari.walker@finovexa.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Aug 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference private deploy — connectivity question

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. NetOps and engineering have a follow-up: we need a recommendation for connectivity into our VPC-hosted Redwood private deployment. Our constraints: PCI-scope workloads, predictable egress bandwidth (~4 Gbps steady with 10 Gbps burst), multi-site (primary DC in NJ, DR in SFO), and a strict ops preference to avoid broad transitive VPC access.

Options on the table from our side:
- VPC Peering between Redwoods' VPC and our app VPCs
- AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints to the service)
- Site-to-site VPN (IPsec, with redundant tunnels)

Questions we care about: encryption and key management, ip addressing impact (no overlapping CIDR), failover behavior across regions, operational blast radius, and unit cost (both month and per-GB). Any high-level recommendation you can provide so we can brief security and procurement?

Appreciate a clear pros/cons list and a preferred path with a fallback.

—Ari
NetOps, Finovexa

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Inference private deploy — connectivity question

Ari — thanks, great summary. Looping in Kim (privacy & private-deploy PM) and Ben (SE) to scope a concise recommendation.

High-level guidance in short: avoid VPC peering for multi-site, PCI-scoped flows due to transitive risks and scaling. Prefer a multipath approach: PrivateLink for control-plane (management/config API) + either Direct Connect (or cloud provider equivalent) or a high-throughput encrypted data path for the data plane. Where dark-fiber/Direct Connect is not possible, run dual site-to-site VPNs with active-passive failover and throughput aggregation.

Ben/Kim — can you add a quick technical delta (bandwidth, failover behavior, cert/KMS model) and I will package a one-pager for Ari's security and procurement teams.

Thanks,
Sean
Senior Solutions Lead

Sean / Kim — quick tech notes (internal):

1) VPC Peering
- Pros: low latency, simple packet path; minimal per-GB cost within-region.
- Cons: Not transitive (so multi-VPC multi-region scales poorly unless you use Transit Gateway), broad routing tables increase blast radius, overlapping CIDR blocks block peering, no native per-flow encryption beyond VPC-level (we still encrypt app traffic TLS).
- Ops: adds burden if Finovexa wants network isolation per environment. For PCI it may be acceptable if scoped to a single VPC pair and strict routing ACLs, but cross-region peering is not supported (must peer regionally).

2) PrivateLink (interface endpoints)
- Pros: Exposes our service on ENIs in the customer's VPC — excellent isolation, removes need to expose public endpoints, compatible with customer NACLs and security controls. Good for control plane and small-volume API traffic.
- Cons: Not designed for very high sustained throughput per endpoint (interface endpoints have ENI/bandwidth limits); cost model is per-hour endpoint + per-GB data processed. For 4 Gbps sustained, cost and scaling become significant (requires multiple endpoints and scaling strategy).
- Ops: Best choice for management/rollouts, webhook/callback traffic, auth/token exchange. Works cleanly with KMS for mutual TLS and customer-managed certs via AWS ACM if they want.

3) Site-to-site VPN (IPsec)
- Pros: Fast to provision, encrypted in transit, supports multi-site via multiple VPN connections and BGP. Can be aggregated across tunnels for bandwidth if vendor/hardware supports (and with ECMP).
- Cons: Bandwidth/cost: cloud VPN gateways often rate-limit at ~1–2 Gbps per tunnel (depends on provider). Maintaining many tunnels increases operational overhead. Repair/failover characteristics depend on routing (BGP timers) and customer CPE.
- Ops: For PCI, you get encryption but need to validate key rotation and endpoint hardening. Recommend customer manages the VPN termination and shares routing with us via BGP.

Recommendation summary (technical):
- Short-term (fast): Deploy PrivateLink for control plane and small API calls + dual site-to-site VPN tunnels to each DC for bulk data, configured with BGP and monitoring. This gets you encrypted transit quickly and keeps blast radius low.
- Mid-term (target): Provision Direct Connect / ExpressRoute equivalent into a transit gateway or our edge (if Finovexa can commit to a port). Use PrivateLink for control plane and Direct Connect for data plane to hit predictable throughput and lower per-GB cost at scale. Include an IPsec overlay to the backup DCs.
- Failover: Use active-active or active-passive BGP depending on traffic patterns; advertise more-specifics for cutovers and monitor RTT/packet-loss thresholds to trigger automated failover.

I'll draft the short one-pager with a diagram (attached) and ballpark numbers on cost.

—Ben

Ari — attaching a short proposal and a diagram that maps to Finovexa's constraints. TL;DR recommendation below and a clear fallback.

TL;DR recommendation (what to present to Security & Procurement)
- Primary path: PrivateLink for control plane + Direct Connect (or provider equivalent) into a Transit Gateway for data plane (predictable costs and performance).
- Fallback / Immediate: PrivateLink (control) + redundant site-to-site IPsec VPNs for data plane. Configure BGP with health-based failover; aggregate traffic where possible.

Why this: PrivateLink minimizes attack surface and respects your desire to avoid transitive VPC exposure; Direct Connect gives predictable egress throughput and lower per-GB cost at scale. VPNs are encrypted and fast to turn up but will require additional operational monitoring and potentially multiple tunnels to reach your bandwidth targets.

Operational notes to include with the one-pager:
- KMS and certificate model: we recommend customer-managed KMS for any PCI-sensitive key material; mutual TLS for application-level traffic; our PrivateLink endpoints can require customer-side endpoint policies.
- Monitoring & SLOs: we deliver token-level latency and per-route cost breakdowns in the Console; we will add synthetic checks across both paths and alert on latency and packet loss thresholds.
- Security review checklist: endpoint policies, NACLs, BGP MD5 for session protection, and quarterly key rotation.

Next steps
1) I attached a 1-page proposal + diagram (20250831-finovexa-connection-proposal.pdf, network-mux-diagram.png).
2) If Security wants, we can run a short workshop to validate routing and cert decisions (30–60m).
3) Procurement: Ben will include a price delta between VPN-only and Direct Connect options once you confirm expected sustained vs burst bytes per month.

If that looks good, feel free to loop in the security procurement alias and we'll schedule the workshop.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference
